meta.document: No county appropriation — Middlesex County government was abolished in 1997
meta.title: Middlesex County — the money that remains
meta.note: Massachusetts abolished Middlesex County government in 1997 (Chapter 48 of the Acts of 1997, approved July 11, 1997) — the county was in fiscal crisis, and its debts and functions were absorbed by the Commonwealth. There is no county budget, no county council, and no county judge. The county-level public money that remains flows two ways: the Middlesex Sheriff's Office, funded by the state, and the Registries of Deeds, funded by recording fees. The budgets that actually shape daily life here — police, schools, roads, trash — are set by the 54 cities and towns and by the state. This page shows the county-level money that still exists; the city layer (Cambridge, Lowell, and more) is being ingested next.

nodes.name: Middlesex County appropriation
nodes.note: There is no county appropriation. Middlesex County government was abolished on July 11, 1997; its functions passed to the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. Here a dead end means the thing itself no longer exists at the county level — the honest answer, not a gap in our records.

nodes.name: Middlesex Sheriff's Office
nodes.note: The one real county-level budget in Middlesex. The Sheriff's Office runs the Middlesex Jail & House of Correction in Billerica and is funded by the Commonwealth through the state budget, not by any county tax — the 4th-largest of Massachusetts's 14 sheriff's offices. Figures are FY2026 enacted (a hair below FY2025's $79,423,908). A separate federal grant, line 8910-0174, adds money outside the state total.

nodes.name: Sheriff's Department — operations
nodes.note: The main operating appropriation for the Middlesex Sheriff's Department, FY2026 enacted.

nodes.name: Retained-revenue & specialized-unit lines
nodes.note: The FY2026 total minus the operations line — the Mental Health Stabilization Unit (8910-1101), Community Programs retained revenue (8910-0450), and Prison Industries retained revenue (8910-1100). In FY2025 these were $1,822,285, $100,000, and $75,000; shown here as their FY2026 combined total pending the line-by-line FY2026 split.

nodes.name: Registries of Deeds (fee-funded)
nodes.note: The Middlesex North (Lowell) and South (Cambridge) Registries of Deeds record property transactions and run on the fees they collect. Their revenue and operating figures are the next county-level pull — from the Registries and the state Comptroller.
